segments.heading: Two phrases you will hear
segments.body: お願いします (onegaishimasu) is used when making a request. ありがとうございます (arigatou gozaimasu) is used when thanking staff. Both are standard polite forms.

segments.heading: Why register matters
segments.body: Standard polite forms are the safe default in a shop. Casual forms belong with friends, not with staff you have not met.

segments.heading: Say it with romaji visible
segments.body: Repeat お願いします with romaji visible. Then cover the romaji and repeat once more; the romaji is a scaffold, not evidence of reading.

worked_example.prompt: You want to ask for a menu politely.
steps: Say お願いします with a small bow
Wait for the staff member to respond
Thank them with ありがとうございます

learner_explanation: Pick the phrase that fits entering a shop and speaking to staff for the first time. Script is shown; romaji is available as a scaffold until you no longer need it.

stimulus.prompt: You walk into a café and the staff look up. Which phrase opens the interaction politely?
choices: ありがとうございます

check.learner_instructions: Choose one phrase. Romaji is shown after your first attempt, not before.

rubric.description: Selects a greeting used when entering a shop
Produces the chosen phrase in Japanese script
Keeps the polite register expected with staff

media.purpose: Show the two phrases side by side in large type
media.spec: two-line card, Japanese script above romaji, high contrast
media.text_equivalent: Card shows お願いします (onegaishimasu) and ありがとうございます (arigatou gozaimasu)
